items.item: Linearizability is a property of a recorded history of invocations and responses, not a property of an algorithm considered in isolation.

at.step: Reveal: every operation takes effect at one instant inside its own interval

items.item: A linearizable history gives each operation the illusion of an instantaneous effect at some point between its invocation and response, and that point must respect real-time precedence: if one operation's response precedes another's invocation, its point must come first.

at.step: Reveal: every operation takes effect at one instant inside its own interval

items.item: Linearizability is a local property: a system is linearizable exactly when every individual object is, which lets objects be verified and implemented independently.

at.step: Reveal: linearizable objects compose, and never make another operation wait

items.item: Linearizability is also a nonblocking property: a pending operation is never required to wait for another to complete.

at.step: Reveal: linearizable objects compose, and never make another operation wait

items.item: A read from a deposed leader can return a stale value even though a completed write has already superseded it, because the deposed leader is unaware a newer leader exists; this breaks the real-time rule and makes the history non-linearizable.

at.step: Hook: a read from the leader, after the leader has already been replaced

items.item: Confirming leadership with a quorum (or bounding a deposed leader's remaining life with a lease) before answering a read removes the stale-leader anomaly.

items.item: Attiya and Welch's model defines d as worst-case network delay and u as worst-case clock/delay uncertainty (0 <= u < d); under synchronized clocks the sum of a read's and a write's worst-case response times is at least d for sequential consistency, and once u is positive, linearizability's per-operation cost floor is roughly u.

items.item: The syllabus phrase 'at least a round trip' is a simplification of the Attiya-Welch result, not the paper's own stated theorem; the exact bound is in terms of d and u and differs across the synchronized and unsynchronized regimes.

items.item: A linearizability checker searches for a total order over a history's operations that is both a legal sequential history of the object and consistent with the history's real-time precedence order; finding none is a formal proof the history is not linearizable.
